newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher on Colombia export hopes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher on Colombia export hopes.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended higher Thursday on talk that Colombia would turn to U.S. supplies to fill at least part of their expected 140,000 tonne rice purchase, traders said.

Colombia is set to import 140,000 tonnes of rice by May 15. U.S. exporters said Colombia would likely buy U.S. or Argentine supplies but added that vessels can reach Colombia faster and cheaper from the U.S. Gulf than from Argentina.
Traders said USDA weekly export sales of 31,500 tonnes were even with the four-week average but were impressive in light of recent sharp price gains.
March rice futures, which were trading at $11.88 per cwt on January 27, closed at $12.26 per cwt on Thursday.
"We're still selling rice at increasingly high prices," one trader said.

Floor sources noted registrations of rice in deliverable locations rose to 1,916,000 cwt as of Thursday. They said they expected 150 to 300 lots to be delivered against March futures on Friday, first notice day for deliveries.
Rice ended two to 14-1/2 cents per cwt higher with March up 12 at $12.26. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 2,000 contracts, against Wednesday's actual volume of 1,611 lots.
